source_basis.predecessor_source_reuse: Pure computational continuation of the predecessor's source-backed exact-tail, curtailment, and mixed-depth model; no new external empirical claim introduced.

tested_model.terminal_rule: commit iff W_r >= k with exact deterministic curtailment
tested_model.objective: maximize worst-position true-commit probability subject to all-null FWER<=.05 and q95 total paired-observation budget

complete_certificate.cost_order_proof: For the listed action order, each action's null conditional no-reject discordant stopping-count distribution first-order stochastically dominates every later action. Componentwise matching of 20 sorted action ranks therefore gives convolution FOSD. Combining FOSD with no-false-commit survival S and target 1-.05/S gives a valid dominance pruning rule for the optimistic q95 necessary bound.
complete_certificate.upper_bound_method: For each exchange-max power level, compute the globally minimal optimistic q95 after Pareto pruning. The optimistic bound assigns every false-commit path zero extra cost, so any multiset with optimistic q95 above a budget is infeasible under every ordering.
complete_certificate.razor_budget_method: At 19 integer budgets the optimistic upper-envelope group was one or two pairs ahead of its exchange-sorted exact q95. For each such budget, all multisets in that power group were checked; exactly one had optimistic q95<=budget. A finite-state DP then maximized the exact all-null pair-cost CDF over every ordering that preserved worst-position power at the group value. This either produced a feasible reordered policy or proved the group infeasible at that budget.
complete_certificate.numerics: Finite binomial/negative-binomial recursions and convolution evaluated in float64; the smallest razor infeasibility margin is over 1e-5, far above accumulated floating rounding observed in normalization checks.

ordering_refinement.interpretation: The exchange ordering maximizes worst-position power for a fixed multiset, but is not always the unique ordering attaining that same maximin value. At three Pareto breakpoints a different power-feasible ordering moves a higher-null-rejection action earlier and reduces q95 pair cost by one or two observations without changing the certified worst-position power.

results: The predecessor's five sampled global certificates extend to a complete exact integer-budget Pareto map for every q95 pair budget from 1800 through 3300 inside the tested action class.
The map has 29 power breakpoints. The large mixed-depth gains around 2000-3250 are not local-search artifacts within this finite model.

Ordering is a second control variable distinct from multiset choice: maximin-power-preserving reorderings can improve cost at razor budgets even when the exchange-sorted order already maximizes power.
No claim is made outside the tested 20-candidate, r in {10,20,30,50}, q=.60 single-good, fresh-audit, exact curtailed upper-tail model.
rejected_or_narrowed_generalizations: Rejected within the tested class: only five sampled budget points were globally certifiable. Every integer budget 1800-3300 is now certified.
Rejected: exchange-sorted ordering is automatically cost-optimal among all orderings that preserve its maximin power. Three breakpoints admit lower-q95 power-preserving reorderings.

Narrowed: the 29-breakpoint map is not a certificate for arbitrary discordant depths, stochastic within-candidate deepening, multiple simultaneous good candidates, different q_good, or non-fresh adaptive audit reuse.
Narrowed: rho=.20 pair-cost robustness still requires the predecessor's predictable sign-clock hazard assumptions when rho varies with history.
